hook.text: Students given lab coats scored higher on attention tests. The same coat called an 'artist smock' had zero effect.

buildup.text: Psychologists Adam and Galinsky coined 'enclothed cognition'—the idea that clothing changes how you think.

discovery.text: Wearing formal clothes increases abstract thinking. Casual clothes promote creative divergence.

twist.text: Uniforms don't just signal role to others—they prime the wearer's own behavior and self-perception.

climax.text: Athletes perform differently in red versus blue jerseys. Color triggers aggression and dominance cues.

punchline.text: You don't just wear clothes. They wear you.

details.summary: Enclothed cognition is the scientifically documented phenomenon where the clothes you wear change how you think and behave. Wearing a lab coat increases attention to detail. A suit boosts abstract thinking. Your wardrobe literally reshapes your mind.
details.whyItMatters: This research proves that dressing for success is more than a cliché. What you put on your body measurably influences your cognitive performance and self-perception.
takeaways: Wearing specific clothing measurably changes cognitive performance
The effect depends on both the garment and its symbolic meaning
Lab coat wearers showed increased sustained attention in studies

faq.question: What was the original enclothed cognition experiment?
faq.answer: In 2012, researchers Adam and Galinsky had participants wear a white coat described as either a doctor's coat or a painter's coat. Those told it was a doctor's coat performed significantly better on attention tasks, showing that symbolic meaning of clothes matters as much as the garment itself.

faq.question: Does enclothed cognition work with casual clothing?
faq.answer: Yes. Studies show that wearing casual clothes can increase creative thinking and reduce inhibition. The key is the symbolic association — if you associate casual wear with freedom and creativity, wearing it can prime those mental states.
